_meta.description: Algorithms that extract surfaces from scalar fields. Marching Cubes walks through voxels finding boundaries. Caves emerge from noise. Landscapes generate portals. The implicit becomes explicit.

beats.concept: A 3D noise field fills invisible space with density values. Marching cubes walks the grid cube by cube — 256 possible configurations, one lookup table — and extracts geometry wherever density crosses a threshold.

beats.concept: Two hundred and fifty-six configurations collapse to fifteen. Every possible corner arrangement — vertex inside or outside — reduces through symmetry to a handful of cases. The lookup table is the entire algorithm.
Seven sculptures stand in a row. Each one computed from the same algorithm, different parameters — sphere, torus, strange attractors made solid.
A cube has eight corners. Each corner is inside or outside. Eight binary states: 256 configurations. For each configuration, a lookup table says where the surface cuts through.
Two modes of summoning form from nothing. The fountain rises — marching cubes extract a vertical shape from a scalar field, geometry crystallizing where density crosses threshold.
Two terrains. Same algorithm, different noise. The flat landscape rolls gently — marching cubes tracing where density crosses zero, converting a scalar field into walkable ground.
Marching cubes at landscape scale. A terrain field — noise-driven, continuous — gets sliced at a threshold. Where the function crosses zero, triangles appear. Ground forms.

Two views of the same algorithm. Outside: terrain stretches under open sky, stone arches rise from the ground like thresholds to nowhere — portals carved by mathematics, not erosion. Inside: the cave closes around you.

Noise becomes architecture. A 3D scalar field — Perlin, simplex, whatever turbulence you choose — fills a volume with densities. Marching cubes walks through, voxel by voxel, checking each corner against a threshold.
Noise evolves. The isosurface chases it.
Each metaball is a point radiating influence. A distance field — strongest at center, fading outward. One sphere alone is trivial. But place two near each other and their fields sum.

A sphere is where distance from center equals radius. Not a mesh. Not vertices. A condition. Implicit surfaces define shape as equation — every point in space returns a signed distance. Negative means inside.
the isosurfaces principle held — carried forward
